front: What are the three types of memory?
back: Register memory - cpu registers Primary/main memory - RAM Secondary memory - disks

front: Explain the difference between the following memory types: DRAM, SRAM, ROM, EEPROM
back: DRAM – Writeable, needs to be refreshed, slow, small (main) SRAM – Writeable, faster, larger (cache) ROM – Read-Only-Memory EEPROM – Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory for persistent storage of temporary information (settings)

front: Briefly describe how data is stored in DVD-ROM.
back: A DVD-ROM stores data as a series of pits burnt into a flat medium, similar to a CD.

front: Explain briefly how it is possible to detect and correct errors on a retrieved data from storage.
back: By adding extra bits and performing a computation to check for invalid sequences.

front: What are the 2 types of RAM?
back: SRAM (Static RAM) — faster, more expensive, used for cache DRAM (Dynamic RAM) — slower, cheaper, used for main memory

front: What are the three main different types of ROM?
back: PROM — programmable once EPROM — erasable and reprogrammable EEPROM — electrically erasable, more flexible

front: What are the three main types of secondary memory?
back: - Magnetic (Hard Disk Drive/magnetic tape) - Optical (CD, DVD, BluRay) - Solid State Storage (SSD, USB, SD cards)

front: What are the 7 layers of the OSI model?
back: 7. Application 6. Presentation 5. Session 4. Transport 3. Network 2. Datalink 1. Physical

front: What are the three main things that two computers needs to communicate?
back: - Physical Connection - Agreed data representation - transfer procedure
A collection of computers that use network PROTOCOLS to exchange data with each other over a network MEDIUM.
